tickets.title: Audit vacuity check: false warnings on generated equations; is random search viable?
tickets.body:
From AoC 2020 day 4 (SW-1249, NOTES-2020.md item 6, ranked 2). The audit's vacuity check tries random inputs and warns when none satisfy a theorem's hypotheses. On day 4 all 8-11 warnings were false, all on compiler-generated equations (heightValid.eq.some with hypothesis value.stripSuffix "cm" = Some number; Spec.validValue.eq.if… with (key == "byr") = True): random texts never hit the literals. Same blindness: check --counterexamples missed a deliberately broken height range (between 151 193). Options raised: (A) skip generated equations in the vacuity check (they come from the definition, so can't be misstated); (B) seed generators with the definition's literals.

D2357 (Matt, 4 Nov): backlog only. Matt doubts random generation is a viable strategy for vacuity at all (hoping it finds inputs); revisit the approach itself (e.g. what a warning should require, or a non-random method) before doing A or B.

From SW-1210 (merged, backlog review 4 Nov 2026), option C: satisfy hypotheses of the form `f x = y` / `f x = Some y` in the counterexample search by computing y from the generated x, so audit tests 'if the program returns X' theorems instead of warning they may be vacuous. From aoc/NOTES-2020.md day 1 item 5: 6 of day 1's 16 theorems gave up this way. Medium, a day or two.
D2306 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): backlog, consider later with evidence from other AoC days (2021/2024/2025 audits will have the same warnings).
Related, kept separate: SW-1063 (custom generators), SW-1247 (generator for non-equation proof fields).

tickets.title: Survey AoC solutions for raw data that should be a domain type (puzzle's language, methods on it)
tickets.body:
The problem: many AoC solutions pass raw structures around (List Bool, List Nat, Pair Nat Nat, List (List Char), tuples) where the puzzle has a noun (a pass, a seat, a cave, a bag rule). The reader has to reconstruct the meaning, and there's no natural home for helper methods. Matt, 4 Nov 2026, generalising day 5's Pass (SW-1282): 'review all of our Advent of Code solutions and see what might be candidates for promoting raw data structures into … a domain object with more significant meaning for that domain … talking about things in the puzzle's language rather than lists of bools or nats … helps make the code more understandable, but possibly also serves as a nice type on which to put helper methods.'

The change: a read-only survey of aoc/src (2020, 2021, 2024, 2025 and Aoc.Common) listing candidates: for each, the raw type and where it flows (program, spec, proofs), the proposed domain type and its methods, a before/after sketch of a few lines, the expected benefit (readability, helper methods, proofs stated in puzzle terms), and the cost/risk (proof churn). Rank them; group shared shapes that belong in Aoc.Common.

What it should do: a ranked list Matt can pick from; each picked candidate becomes its own refactor lane (as SW-1282 did for day 5).

Rule added to CLAUDE.md the same day (lane agents: domain types in application code).

Done (Sonnet, ~5 min, est. 60): docs/research/aoc-domain-types.md: 30 candidates (6 high, 11 medium, 13 low), 5 shared shapes, 26 days fine as they are. D2363 recorded on the follow-up tickets.

tickets.title: Design note: Scala-style partial-function lambdas (collect) in Stitchwort
tickets.body:
D2368 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): a match whose result is Option does NOT silently default missing cases to None; keep the exhaustiveness check, be explicit. But Matt wants Scala's partial-function vibe ('map with a partial function based on your match, emit things that don't match ... very high expressivity'): xs.collect { case ... => ... }. Orchestrator's sketch: (1) clause lambdas, a lambda written as match arms; (2) an explicitly marked partial form that desugars to a match whose arms are wrapped in Some with a final _ => None, so it fits List.filterMap / a new List.collect (a → Option b); partiality is opt-in and visible, so the exhaustiveness check stays everywhere else. Questions for the note: syntax (fits lambda-syntax.md's grammar, the | ambiguity in one-line matches), how it reads in pipelines, Option vs a dedicated PartialFn with isDefinedAt, guards, other uses (Map.collect, Parse alternatives, orElse chaining), what proofs see (it is an ordinary match; collect membership lemma), and survey of AoC sites that would use it.
Progress (lane, 4 Nov 22:18): note written, docs/proposals/partial-lambdas.md (commit 3665220a1 on lane/SW-1292). Recommends design B: `match | …` clause lambdas (total), `match? | …` (arms wrapped in Some, rest None; for filterMap/findMap), `matches | …` (Boolean side, Scala's cond; rest False, body-less arm = True); guards `| p if c => e` as a later stage. Rejects C (partial by callee type) and D (PartialFn record). Decisions P1-P10 for Matt. Survey: 10 pipeline sites (5 need guards), 10 Option tables, 12 total clause lambdas, Boolean form 6 aoc + 13 std.

Merged as a proposal; awaiting Matt's decisions P1–P10 (asked as D2370: accept the recommendations?). Model result: Opus, worked, 11 min (+ the cond addition) (est. 60).

D2370 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): 'I really like this.' Spelling: match | … (total clause lambda), match some | … (Some for listed cases, None otherwise), matches | … (true for listed cases, false otherwise); replaces the note's match?. Other recommendations accepted; guards (P3) being discussed as D2371.

D2371 (Matt): guards yes, as a follow-on stage after SW-1294 (ticket filed).

tickets.title: Pattern guards (| p if c => e) in every match; follows SW-1294
tickets.body:
D2371 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): yes, as a follow-on stage after SW-1294. Stage 4 of docs/proposals/partial-lambdas.md (§6): | p if c => e in match … with, definition arms, and the three new forms (match, match some, matches). When the guard is false the arms below are tried; a guarded arm covers nothing for exhaustiveness (E-NONEXHAUSTIVE), so ordinary matches still need an unguarded arm, while match some / matches' hidden default covers the rest. Compiles to an if in the case tree whose else continues with the remaining arms; W-REDUNDANT with guarded arms; proofs see an ordinary if. Revives SW-237 (pruned without a note). Plan: Opus checks the design (a short note revising SW-237), then Sonnet implements; then migrate the five guarded pipeline sites (2024 days 6, 15, 20; 2021 day 18). Est. 3-4 h. Starts after SW-1294 merges.

Design note docs/proposals/pattern-guards.md (Opus, 15 min). Orchestrator's calls (minor, per Matt's overnight rule): (1) ship guards before generated equations exist (arms from the first guarded one get no equations/f.induct, E-NO-EQUATION with the reason); equations in a separate Opus lane; (2) migrate only 2024 day 15 positionsOf and 2021 day 18 orderedPairs (the others read better as filter/map); (3) guards may not perform operations (E-ABILITY), can be relaxed later. Implementation: Sonnet, same branch, est. 3-4 h.

Implemented (Sonnet, ~50 min, est. 210). Departure from the note: the kernel allows case only at the top of a body or branch, so the compiler makes the splits later rows need above the guard; the else tree holds only guards, leaves and missing cases. New E-GUARD-ARMS (absurd arm below a guard), E-MATCH-SIZE. AoC: 2024 d15 positionsOf, 2021 d18 orderedPairs. Opus review started 00:45 (generates kernel terms); day 18's audit went 15 -> 16 vacuity warnings, to explain. Findings: note §3.2 to correct; 'b != 0 && c != 0' gives no b ≠ 0 fact in an if (possible SW-226 gap).

Opus review (01:05): arm selection right on every input tried (columns, nested, literals, Vec/Fin, captures). Blocking: E-MALFORMED in the kernel when an arm below a guard is itself a match (in_tree not switched off for the else's leaves). Fix before merge: indexed-family matches falsely non-exhaustive after a guard; false E-GUARD-ARMS for nested (). Also: size limit too low for linear shapes; a misleading E-NO-EQUATION hint; note §3.2/§4 corrections. Sent back to the Sonnet lane (est. 60 min). Conjunction facts filed as SW-1305.

Review fixes done (7decb219e, d04608994): match bodies below a guard lifted; indexed missing cases tried with empty_case (and an impossible branch's guarded arms still type-checked); unit pattern below a guard; E-MATCH-SIZE 4096; hint and note corrections. Opus re-review of 7decb219e: nothing blocking, one fix (unchecked arm in an impossible branch), done in d04608994 (checks the chain first, then uses the empty-type term; reviewed by the orchestrator, not re-reviewed by Opus). Model result: Sonnet, needed fixes (kernel E-MALFORMED below a guard; indexed exhaustiveness; nested unit; an unchecked arm in an impossible branch, all found by the Opus review), ~100 min (est. 210).

tickets.title: if p && q (and auto generally) doesn't give each conjunct: 'if b != 0 && c != 0 then a % b' is E-AUTO-STUCK
tickets.body:
Found in the SW-1295 review, confirmed on main: neither an if on a conjunction nor auto splits p ∧ q into its parts, so 'if b != 0 && c != 0 then a % b else 0' fails with E-AUTO-STUCK (can't decide b ≠ 0); also with ∧, ≠ and b > 0 && c > 0. SW-226 only promised the right side of && knows the left. Applies to guards too ('| x if p && q =>'). Likely small in auto: split conjunction hypotheses.

DeepSeek attempt (branch ds/SW-1305, 18c225a1b; ~60 min) works on the examples but not merged: beyond its brief it changed how every 'if b && c' on propositions elaborates (both branches elaborated twice, the conjunction form kept only if a branch's auto proof uses it; doubling cost for nested ifs) and refactored unused_proof_if, which conflicts with SW-1295's check_if. Orchestrator's call: rerun on Opus, using the attempt as a reference. Model result: DeepSeek, failed (went past the brief's limit into a general change to if; design-level), 60 min (est. 60).

Opus lane (lane/SW-1305, f98bc2c74; started 02:01, done ~02:36, est. 90 min). The Bool reading of `a && b` records on the way the conjunction its operands decide (decided props, or a Bool c as c = True; at least one prop; b not using a's proof) with decision `Decidable.andThen da (_ => db)` (new std def, short-circuits like &&). `if` on it goes through the decided path like `if b != 0`; unused proof → the recorded Bool reading, so terms unchanged (prelude snapshot: only the two new defs added). One elaboration of the condition and branches. auto: parts of conjunction hypotheses (And.left/right, 8 deep) as a last step. Checks: elab lane, examples+hashes for auto-conjunction/pattern-guard, binary(hash_stability), std self-tests, aoc + rogue check: all pass. Bench: the check-number-*/text-literal/nested-parens "regressions" are identical on main without the change (stale baseline). Not covered: `if n != 0 && len % n == 0 then len / n` (b uses a's proof; needs a dependent conjunction), proof-valued ifs (check_proof_if keeps the Bool form).

Done on Opus (f98bc2c74, 35 min, est. 90): logic::condition records a ∧ b and a decision (new std Decidable.andThen/andYes) while reading a && b as Bool; check_if_in then takes the same path as 'if b != 0' (unused proof falls back to the original Bool term, so no hash moves; prelude snapshot gains the two new functions); auto tries conjunction parts last, depth 8. Guards benefit. Not covered: 'if n != 0 && len % n == 0' (dependent conjunction). Orchestrator's calls (minor): a Bool operand reads as c = True inside a conjunction, keep; the two std functions, yes. Bench drift is the stale 2 Nov baseline (identical with the change stashed).

Merged 2f7bf899b; verified: merge tier 1078/1078, hashes, fmt, natives, std_library, guide, aoc check and 1364 tests, rogue, audit. Model result: Opus, worked, 35 min (est. 90).

tickets.title: A list literal [f x, ..rest] in a recursive result compiles to plain recursion, where Cons (f x) rest becomes a loop (tail recursion modulo cons); and it elaborates to a different term (hashes differ)
tickets.body:
Found by SW-1256's verifier: with List.map written [f x, ..List.map xs f], extract's more_tail_calls_are_loops overflowed the JS stack on 1,000,000 elements. List.map, takeWhile, spanOnto reverted to Cons on main. Find why a list literal with a spread doesn't elaborate to the same Cons term (SW-1221 noted the hash difference), make it do so, or make codegen see the loop; then convert those three back. Other converted sites (Parse, Reads, Terminal, aoc) may also have lost loops: check generated code for each.

Done on lane/SW-1324 (75e1e06d9; Sonnet, 41 min, est. 75). Cause: in a computation, a list literal went through comp_compound's infer, which wrapped the constructor in an annotation the JS loop detection didn't see; Cons went through comp_call as a constructor-as-lambda application. Fix (effects.rs): check Expr::List against the expected type; new comp_ctor_app builds a fully applied constructor from its fields' results. Now both forms are the same term; List.map, takeWhile, spanOnto back to brackets; 130 hash snapshots move (List.map's users). Changes elaboration of constructors in computations, so an independent Opus review started 06:45. Model result: Sonnet, worked, 41 min (est. 75). Finding: comp_app still uses the lambda form for named or partial constructor applications with a performing argument (low priority).

Review (Opus, 12 min): one blocking regression, fixed in de90f4a6f: a performing comparison in a constructor's Bool field (MkFlag (len() < 3)) wasn't decided; fields now go through run_argument with their slot types, as in comp_app. Order, once-only, implicit, dependent and proof fields, and the List check all held. Pre-existing gap filed as SW-1325.

Merged 9bfa4b6b5; verified: merge tier 1081, hashes, extract 60/60, std tests, aoc check and 1368 tests, rogue check and 100 tests, full audit.

Found by the SW-1330 Opus review (repro: scratchpad sw1330-review/r5, r6). B uses rewrite inside Option.map and needs Option.mapCong (Option/Lemmas.sw), which only A loads. Change A so it no longer loads that file: fresh, B fails ('there is no Option.mapCong'); cached, B is reported from its entry. Fix: lazy loading must behave as if every file were loaded: the congruence/auto lookups should treat a pending name as something to load (or the loader counts F.…Cong as needed when F is referenced). Priority: correctness of check. Sonnet (Opus if the loader design needs it).

Done on lane/SW-1354 (1bf291ea6): congruence lemmas must sit in their function's file (index refuses others; 4 moved, Ring.mulCong renamed Int.mulCong); auto's library decision procedures are per namespace (its own references' files + its dependencies'), set on check and replay. No extra loading; aoc check --no-cache CPU within noise. Orchestrator's call (implementation detail): keep 'beside their function, enforced' over loading lemma files with F's. Model result: Opus, worked, 27 min (est. 120). Next: rebase SW-1330 and rerun its blocker.sh.

tickets.title: Design note: range syntax (a ..< b, a ..= b, or other), after a thorough survey of other languages (Swift, Rust, Kotlin, Haskell, Python, Scala, Ruby, Julia, Lean, Idris, Agda, F#, Elixir …)
tickets.body:
D2403 (Matt, 5 Nov): yes, an Opus lane; 'definitely do a thorough search of existing languages to see what other people do, including Swift, Rust, Kotlin, etc.' Prompted by List.range (Int.toNat target.right). Constraint: .. already means spread in brackets ([x, ..rest]), so Haskell's [2..n] would clash. Cover inclusive/exclusive, Nat/Int/Char, steps and counting down, List vs lazy, membership lemma (x ∈ a ..< b ↔ a ≤ x < b, pairs with chained comparisons), patterns, Fin, loops, and the List.range argument-order question (SW-1258). Opus, ~45 min. Next free slot.

Done on lane/SW-1356 (30797b999): docs/proposals/ranges.md. 25-language survey with sources; ~1,100 range sites (578 of aoc's 679 in proofs). Recommends a ..< b and a ..= b as List.range a b; no [a..b]. Decisions R1–R9 asked as D2405–D2413. Model result: Opus, worked, 8 min (est. 45).

Matt, 5 Nov 2026: 'I approve the range syntax of Stitchwort. Please cue that for implementation.' D2405-D2413 all as recommended: a ..< b and a ..= b, no bare .. or [a..b] (error names both) (D2405); both forms, ..= b is ..< b + 1 (D2406); a range is a List, the call List.range a b (D2407); List.range (from) (until) replaces one-arg List.range and List.between, rangeFrom stays (D2408); Nat then Int by type, Char later (D2409); reversed is empty, .reverse to count down, no step syntax (D2410); Bool x in a ..< b decided by comparisons (D2411); no range patterns now (D2412); W-RANGE-IN-BRACKETS (D2413). Implementation: steps 1-5 of docs/proposals/ranges.md §13, one after another.

D2454 (Matt, 6 Nov 2026): yes (SW-1584 Runs lemmas, a two-day trial, then decide on a sweep; close SW-1229), on condition that a brief literature review first confirms Reads/Runs follows established patterns for verified parsers ('if we're doing something very standard, then yeah, let's proceed'). Started on Opus, analysis only, expected: 40 min.

Done (2b04e78d8), merged: docs/research/parser-proofs-literature.md, 15 sources (8 read in full). Verdict: standard. Reads/Runs match the soundness/completeness theorems of Vermillion and Jourdan-Pottier-Leroy; Written is a Narcissus-style format relation; Declines is the usual PEG choice rule. Differences: proofs built by hand per day from combinator lemmas (as Danielsson/EverParse/Narcissus, which automate it); uniqueness comes almost free from completeness + determinism; round trip with a printer is the other spec style. D2454's condition met. Model result: Opus, worked, 6 min (est. 40).

tickets.title: Native lowering: a call's arguments are copied instead of moved when sibling argument blocks reuse register slots, so the copies keep cells shared (dijkstra: 100% of queue insert steps, 50% of map inserts); repro: pop-then-insert loop on a Set
tickets.body:
From SW-2382 (relaxEdges pc 49 passes root children as copies; best.insert at pc 64 moves). Likely most of SW-2371's 17%. Repro and counting patch: /private/tmp/claude-550/-Users-agent-repos-mdr-stitchwort/8230e28a-2fab-4832-920d-c5160adb7e00/scratchpad/micro/p1.sw, counting2.patch. 60-90 min.

Started 06:02 UTC, Opus, expected 90 min.


Lane (Opus, 06:31, ~30 min): cause was the use sets in `crates/rt/src/code.rs` (`fill`): they counted reads of slots bound *inside* an expression (by a `let` or match arm), and sibling scopes share slots, so a later sibling's own variable made an earlier sibling's last read look live: copy, not move. Fix: a `let` drops its slot from its body's uses, a match arm its field slots. Native takes MOVE marks from the bytecode, so both back ends are fixed. Commit 1c4a7b47d on lane/SW-2388, with test `machine::arguments_are_moved_past_siblings_sharing_slots` (fails before, passes after). p1 micro: shared unpacks 1.66 M to 0.47 M (insertWith, minView all unique; what's left is `shape`'s read and doubleL/R). Native instructions: dijkstra 48.41 G to 43.99 G (-9.1%), memory-game 34.06 G to 33.44 G (-1.8%), binary-trees 30.08/30.06 G, expressions 540.2/539.9 G. Tests: lane rt 60/60, lane native 55/55, bench:compare:check 66 ok, clippy clean. Step counts unchanged (charged per call/frame, not per instruction).

Merged (orchestrator reviewed soundness: only slots rebound by an inner binder are left out; a correct packer rebinds only dead slots). dijkstra 48.41 -> 43.99 G instructions (-9.1%), memory-game -1.8%. Step counts unchanged. Model result: Opus, worked, 30 min (est. 90).

21:22: done, lane/SW-2439 5893f8d88. Minimal: `let f := ((i, s)) => i + s.size` then `f (1, Circle 4) == 5` (no annotation; both the waiting `.size` and the waiting `==` needed). tickets.title: Zonk's let fold-back matches syntactically and misses when operator specialisation differs (generic + with dictionary vs Nat.add); make it robust, then SW-2439's head annotation may become unnecessary. Also check siblings: lift.rs:1028 helper lifting, Proj of an inlined constructor value, an inlined match applied
tickets.body:

From SW-2570. Repro: STITCHWORT_EFFECT_FUZZ_SEED=1794200310 STITCHWORT_EFFECT_FUZZ_BATCHES=1 cargo test --release -p stitchwort-cli --test extraction effect_differential::generated -- --nocapture (dump the module). Possibly exponential evaluation of open Nat terms. Profile first. 120 min.

Started 10 Nov 00:55 (est. 120 min), on lane/SW-2572 (Opus).

10 Nov 01:45, to review. Profile (macOS `sample`, seed 1794200310 shrunk to `let a := if (x + 500000) % 2 == 0 then 4 else 4; if a % 2 == 0 ...`): all the time in `native::as_nat_with` forcing already-unfolded calls under the elaborator's obligations loop. Cause: `(x + k) % 2` multiplies a quotient of k/2 `Succ`s around a stuck step by 2; `*` peels one `Succ` a step, and at each step `native::run` walked the rest of the chain to see it wasn't a number: quadratic in k. Not exponential, not let sharing. Fix (core, `native.rs`, so the kernel computes this way too; docs/core.md updated; needs an Opus review per D2364): `Nat.mul`'s shortcut for unknowns, `(k + m) * n = k*n + m * n` for a number n, in one step; and `native::run` checks every number argument's head before walking a `Succ` chain, so `(k + m) * y` with y unknown is linear too. What's equal is unchanged. Timings (user s): `(x + 16000) % 2` 10.1 -> 0.46, `((x+16000)/2)*y` 9.2 -> 0.56; seed 1794200310's module >10 min -> 4.3 s; the other four seeds 1.0-1.5 s; 200 fuzzer batches from 1794200000 in 51 s, none skipped. Tests: new `resources::remainders_of_long_numbers_check_in_linear_time` (1.5 s), Mul added to `natives::shortcuts_with_unknowns_agree_with_the_definitions` (a mutated shortcut fails it), `a_batch_the_checker_cannot_finish_stops_at_the_deadline` deadline 5 s -> 1 s (the seed now checks in about 4 s). Lanes core, elab, effects, hashes pass. Left: `Nat.divFuel` still builds a quotient one `Succ` a step (linear, ~13 us per unit: `(x + 500000) % 2` forced fully takes 7 s); a divFuel shortcut would be a new kernel shortcut, proposed as a follow-up.

Done 10 Nov. Cause: (x + k) % 2's quotient is k/2 Succs around a stuck division; Nat.mul peeled one per step and native::run re-walked the chain each time (quadratic). Fix (native.rs, kernel): (k + m) * n -> k·n + m * n in one step when m starts with a Succ; head checks before Succ walks. Opus review: sound, F1-F4 fixed (docs/reviews/SW-2572-nat-mul-shortcut-review.md). Seed 1794200310 > 10 min -> 4.3 s; 200 batches 51 s, none skipped. Follow-ups SW-2603 (divFuel), SW-2604 (budget for Succ walks), SW-2605 (deadline test input). Model result: Opus, worked, 47 + 20 + 15 min (est. 120).

So memory pressure is NOT needed; the common point is names_and_proofs (typed_binds). Job 51's crashing tests passed this time.


Lane (Opus, 9 Nov 22:56-23:06, est. 120 min): no bug found in Stitchwort's code; best lead is a Linux kernel bug. The crash path (CLI main -> host::stack::run_on thread -> LibraryIndex::build -> decl_refs -> names_and_proofs) is safe Rust over a freshly parsed, self-owning AST (ast::Name owns its String). The CLI has no other live thread then (main is in pthread_join; the other spawns in elab/core are test-only), and no native code has run yet. The only unsafe code or FFI on the path is host::stack (reviewed: sound, also under musl's TLS-on-supplied-stack), musl and mimalloc v3.3.2 (libmimalloc-sys 0.1.49 builds v3 by default).
Lead: Linux 7.0 to 7.1.8 and 7.2-rc1 to rc6 have a bug in page-table reclaim (CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM, def_bool y, used on MADV_DONTNEED): zap_pte_range flushes the wrong address when it frees an empty PTE table, so a CPU can keep a stale paging-structure-cache entry to a freed table. Writes get lost, pages read back as zero, pointers go bad, in a single thread too. It's worst on AMD (EFER.TCE) and on Intel with INVPCID and KPTI off. Introduced by 4c640eb4181c (v7.0); fixed by torvalds/linux 478a1c3abebf "mm: fix incorrect flush address in direct page table reclaim" (5 Aug 2026; in v7.2-rc7, v7.2, and stable v7.1.9 and later; v7.0.14 is still unfixed). Ref: BurntSushi/ripgrep#3494, the same symptoms in musl builds. mimalloc v3 purges freed memory with MADV_DONTNEED 1 s after it's freed (prim/unix/prim.c _mi_prim_decommit; purge_delay 1000), and LibraryIndex::build runs just after a second of parsing churn. That fits: no memory pressure needed, Linux only, never on Speedwell (macOS), wrong results as well as crashes.
To confirm on Overmind: uname -r; zcat /proc/config.gz | grep PT_RECLAIM; cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/vulnerabilities/meltdown; lscpu | grep 'Vendor ID'. If the kernel is in the affected range: as a diagnostic, rerun job 51's failing tests with MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=-1 exported (stops mimalloc's MADV_DONTNEED). The fix is a kernel of 7.1.9 or later, 7.2 or later, or the 6.18 LTS (Matt's host config). No code change, no regression test (a kernel bug).

Orchestrator, 23:10: asked Overmind for uname/config/CPU (lane done in 10 min, no code change). Waiting on its answer before going further.

Overmind, 23:12: kernel 6.18.60 (before the 7.0 regression), CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM=y, Intel, PTI on. So the kernel lead is dead. Next (lanes mode, Opus): a Linux ASan build of the CLI and test binaries for job 51's failing set; or that set with mimalloc swapped for the system allocator, to see whether the crashes follow mimalloc. Parked overnight (orchestrator's call): the remaining causes are mimalloc, musl or the compiler, and that needs Overmind time we've given to the night checks.

tickets.title: [Opus] Conversion keeps ~1.6 KB per unfolded level of a decreasing-checked recursion (innerN 2^128: 3.3 GB before the 2M-frame E-RESOURCE); shrink what Unfolding retains, or unfold lazily (fuzz_elab 0x25a5 case 4273)
tickets.body:
Found by Overmind, fuzz_elab CASES=12000 seed 0x25a5, 10 Nov 2026. Input on Overmind: target/fuzz-elab/25a5-4273.sw. Est. 60 min.

Lane notes (Sonnet, 10 Nov 2026): not fixed; cause found, needs a decision or Opus. The check already stops with a clear E-RESOURCE ("recursed more deeply than allowed", 4 s) but only at the evaluator's 2,000,000-frame limit, with 3.3 GB resident. Path: `unify_step` -> `unfold_folded` -> `force_now` -> `value::run`: conversion unfolds `innerN 2^128` (a `decreasing` function, so a fuelled helper) to head normal form before comparing with `innerN 0`'s. Every level pushes a `Frame::Unfolded` (64 bytes) and keeps its `Unfolding` and the helper's per-level values alive: about 1.6 KB per frame (measured: `innerN 200000` succeeds in 3 s and 744 MB, linear in n). A structural recursion of the same shape (no `decreasing`) is cheap (200000 deep: 0.3 s, 147 MB), so the weight is the `decreasing` helper's per-level terms. Not the work limit (10^10 steps, never reached), not postponed problems or a cache, not SW-2467's pattern chain. The options (unlowering `Limits::frames` for elaboration-time conversion only; a bytes-based cap; making conversion unfold lazily one step; shrinking the per-level retention) change what elaboration accepts or touch crates/core, so they are not done here.
Diagnosis (Sonnet lane, 10 Nov): not the step budget; conversion (unify_step -> unfold_folded -> force_now -> value::run) unfolds innerN 2^128 to head normal form, one Frame::Unfolded per level, until the 2M-frame limit gives E-RESOURCE after 4 s and 3.3 GB. ~1.6 KB retained per level (frames are 64 bytes): the unfolding data and the decreasing helper's per-level values. Without decreasing the same recursion costs 147 MB at 200k. Ruled out: postponed problems, caches, SW-2467's chain, SW-2418. Moved to Opus: shrink the retention (crates/core Unfolding) or unfold lazily.

Lane notes (Opus, 10 Nov 2026, stopped early at the orchestrator's restart; no code committed): cause confirmed with a heap profile (malloc_history at 300,000 frames) and a frame census. Two `Frame::Unfolded` per level (`innerN.%go`, `innerN.%step`), so the 2M-frame limit is hit at 1M levels. The frames themselves are small (64 B + a 128 B `Unfolding` each). The bulk (~3 KB/level) is the proof chain: `%go`'s `%rec` passes `Nat.leTrans (Succ y) (m x) k p h`, which holds the previous level's `h`, so every level's proof stays reachable from the innermost environment however the frames go. Each link is a glued `leTrans` call (5-arg spine: Rc 192 B + spill to capacity 8, ~640 B; plus an `Unfolding`) and `p` = `Omega.prove` (6-arg spine, same cost) with its certificate's constructor values rebuilt each level (~880 B, mostly closed terms). Measured (release, --no-cache): 2^128 with decreasing 4.8 s / 3.31 GB; without decreasing 0.83 s / 466 MB (2M levels); 200,000 with decreasing 3.1 s / 744 MB, without 0.32 s / 147 MB. Shrinking alone can't reach the goal: boxing `Unfolding`'s kept value (tried, reverted) saved only 3% (3.22 GB); exact-size spines and sharing closed certificate parts might reach ~2 KB/level at best, against ~470 B needed. Eliding frames for unshared unfoldings would make the loop tail-recursive and run on to the 10^10-step budget with the chain still growing: worse. Lazy proof arguments still chain through environments (~800 B/level est.) and are a large kernel change. So reaching the goal needs either a memory cap on a check (option 3: changes what's accepted, so Matt's call, like the frame limit) or a `decreasing` encoding whose proof doesn't chain (changes hashes; none found). Next: write this up as docs/reviews/SW-2639-decreasing-memory.md with a D question (memory cap?), ~30 min. Instrumentation used (pause at a frame count, names of frames, system allocator for malloc_history) was not committed.
Paused 10 Nov for a session restart. Next: write docs/reviews/SW-2639-decreasing-memory.md (cause: decreasing proof chain via Nat.leTrans holds every level's h, ~3 KB/level; frames are small) with a D question on a per-check memory cap (Opus, ~30 min). Branch lane/SW-2639 deleted after merge (only the note).

Write-up (Opus, 10 Nov 2026, paper lane, ~10 min): docs/reviews/SW-2639-decreasing-memory.md. Found a non-chaining encoding: `f.%go`'s recursive call decides `Nat.leq (Succ (m y)) k` afresh and passes the match's `found` (rfl at run time); the old `h` and `p` appear only in the impossible branch. Kernel and runtimes unchanged, hashes of decreasing defs change. Hand-written model, 200,000 levels with an omega proof: chained 3.0 KB/level (671 MB), fresh check 0.86 KB/level (251 MB), time about the same (measured). Memory cap not recommended (bytes differ native vs wasm). D3474 (number to confirm): adopt the fresh-check encoding? [rec: yes, ordinary Opus lane]. Parked speed findings: argument lists spilled at capacity 8; closed omega certificate values rebuilt per level.
Write-up merged (10 Nov): docs/reviews/SW-2639-decreasing-memory.md. Recommends D3474: generated fuel helper decides Nat.leq (Succ (m y)) k afresh at each call (proof rfl), old proofs only in the impossible branch; model 3.0 -> 0.86 KB/level; kernel unchanged; hashes of decreasing defs change. No memory cap.

The problem: the salt that should stop 'a cache copied from elsewhere (a committed .stitchwort, a download)' (docs/proposals/check-cache.md §3.1) is read from check/header inside the cache directory (crates/driver/src/check_cache.rs:149-173), so a whole directory that arrives with a project fits. Entries are sealed with plain BLAKE3, no secret. Loaded entries go through admit_trusted_*, which skips type and termination checking. check, test and audit all read the cache by default (crates/cli/src/main.rs:1440-1451, 2690, 2727).

Confirmed: cp -Rp a checked project with its .stitchwort to another folder and check there; the std.* entries keep their modification times, so they were read from the copy, not rebuilt.
Not confirmed: a forged entry proving False (needs the encoder in crates/elab/src/cache/codec.rs).

Fix, one of: (a) seal each entry with a keyed hash whose key is per user and outside any project; (b) audit always checks in full, and check-cache.md says a cache directory is as trusted as the compiler. A trust decision: Matt's.
Also (SW-2672 G3, cache/mod.rs:2671-2688): after a replay, the entry's stated hashes are installed without being computed; later entries' dependency checks trust them. Fix: a mode, on in tests and audit, that recomputes and refuses a mismatch. Part of D3475.

tickets.title: Kernel: a data type becomes final with an index type that mentions a failed declaration
tickets.body:
Severity 3 (missing guard), from SW-2659 (docs/reviews/SW-2659-kernel-soundness-audit.md, F2).

declare_indexed_data_group lets a failed reference through in the parameters and index types ('define_data_group finds it again', crates/core/src/check.rs:2815, 2832). admit_data_group re-checks the parameters, fields and result indices (check.rs:3087, 3113, 3223) but not the members' index telescopes. So a group whose index type mentions a failed definition, with fields and result indices that don't, becomes final, against admissible's invariant (check.rs:3483) and docs/core.md ('nothing built on it is ever accepted').

No path to False found: the failed definition is a neutral constant and anything mentioning it directly is still refused. No CLI repro (the surface can't write it).

Fix: in admit_data_group, pass every member's index types to the first admissible call. A core test: a failed definition in an index type, no constructors, must fail with E-FAILED-DEPENDENCY.


Progress (10 Nov, Opus lane, 943deae32): guard added in admit_data_group (every member's index types join the first admissible call). Test admission::an_index_type_that_uses_a_failed_declaration_fails_the_type (fails without the guard: "ok"). docs/core.md admission rule now names index types and result indices.

tickets.title: Kernel: a data type's parameter types aren't checked for case outside a case tree
tickets.body:
Severity 3 (missing guard), from SW-2659 (docs/reviews/SW-2659-kernel-soundness-audit.md, F3).

Signatures, fields, indices and result indices all go through case_only_in_tree(ty, false) (crates/core/src/check.rs:2303, 3105, 2836, 3228). A data group's parameter types don't, in declare_indexed_data_group (check.rs:2815-2821) or admit_trusted_data_decls (check.rs:3378-3403). check accepts a Case wherever it is checked against a type (a lambda body in an argument: check.rs:438, 541), and a case outside a definition's tree that gets stuck panics (crates/core/src/value.rs:2482).

Only a wrong elaborator or cache entry reaches it; the result is a panic, not a false theorem.

Fix: the same check on each parameter type in both functions, with a core test.


Progress (10 Nov, Opus lane with SW-2674, 943deae32): case_only_in_tree on each parameter type in declare_indexed_data_group and admit_trusted_data_decls. Test admission::a_parameter_type_cannot_hold_a_case covers both paths (without the guard it panics at value.rs:2482).

tickets.body:
Found by SW-2812. Repro:
```
import Std (Bool, Eq, Nat)

theorem c (m: Nat) (n: Nat) (h: Nat.equal m n = True): (if m = n then 1 else 0) = 1 :=
  rewrite h in rfl
```

Progress (11 Nov, Opus lane): cause found and fixed. The usual motive fails (the decision's `sound` is typed by `Nat.equal m n = True`), so rewrite carries `Nat.decEq`'s proofs along the equation (carry.rs). Its proofs are lambdas (`h => Nat.equalSound m n h`), and carrying built the redexes `(h => S) e` and `(h => C) h'`; the kernel can't infer a lambda's type, so checking the motive failed with the kernel's E-CANNOT-INFER. Only decisions whose proofs are calls (as in rewrite-decision-plain-first) worked. Fix in `Carry::carried`: a lambda `sound` takes the carried proof through a `let` typed `s = True`; a lambda `complete` takes its argument, a variable, by substitution. Example examples/accept/rewrite-decision-lambda-proofs.sw with its hash snapshot. Tests: the repro checks; EXAMPLES=rewrite-decision-lambda-proofs,rewrite-decision running examples tests 3/3 pass; hash_stability::examples for the new example passes. Commit 8405657db.

tickets.title: G2 reread walks a right-nested chain to the bottom at every comparison level: quadratic in depth, and for a chain with no folded call (rep 10000 x, k * x in the plain evaluator) the walk costs no budget steps (~10^8 uncounted visits at depth 10,000). Measure a depth-10,000 chain; if it matters, charge a step per level or make the walk iterative (which also makes the E-RESOURCE depth independent of build profile). Also: the stack error's wording ('nested too deeply for the conversion'; Depth would match same_spines). Review: docs/reviews/SW-2874-g2-nested-sums-review.md 3c, 4c, 7
tickets.body:
Estimate: 75 min (started 16:51, done 17:25).

Progress (Opus lane, 11 Nov 2026). Measured first, release CLI, `check --no-cache`, STITCHWORT_TIMINGS (elab ms / kernel ms / steps for the theorem). Probes: `repEnd n x e` (structural, `x + repEnd k x e`), equal (`repEnd D x y = repEnd (D-1) x (x + y)`) and unequal (`... y = ... z`); `decreasing` `f (Succ k) y = y + f k y`, equal (`x + f D y = x + (y + f (D-1) y)`) and unequal (`f D` against `f (D-1)`).

Before:
- rep equal 1,000: 88 / 83 ms, 129k steps. 10,000: 7,550 / 7,356 ms, 1.29M steps, 15.3 s wall. Profile: `reread_with` (unifier and kernel). Quadratic and uncounted, as the review said.
- dec equal 10,000: 268 / 301 ms, 13.5M steps (fine). dec unequal 10,000: 33,219 ms elab, 14.8M steps, 33.7 s; profile again `reread_with` in the unifier.
- rep unequal 1,000: 3,443 ms, 90M steps; 10,000 > 60 s. Not reread: the profile is `refl_error` -> `Ctx::show` evaluating for the message (finding, below).

Change: `nat_add::reread` is a loop (no Rust recursion, so no `nesting("conversion")` and no profile-dependent E-RESOURCE from it; review 4c and 7 gone), charges `budget.step()` per sum it goes down to (not the top one), and takes an `Unread` record: the sums a walk found nothing to unfold in, by spine address (values kept). A later walk stops at one. Kept per outermost `conv` (in its `CallMemo`) and per outermost unification (in the unifier's `CallMemo`, valid while `effects` — epoch, trail length, postponed — is unchanged); `case`s and the reference evaluator pass a fresh one. Off with the shortcuts off. docs/core.md rule E says so.

After:
- rep equal 1,000: 4 / 3 ms, 133k steps. 10,000: 86 / 34 ms, 1.33M steps, 0.36 s wall (was 15.3 s).
- dec equal 10,000: 351 / 304 ms, 13.6M steps. dec unequal 10,000: 628 ms, 15.0M steps, 1.1 s (was 33.7 s).
- 50,000 (all three kinds): E-RESOURCE "recursed more deeply than allowed ... while unfolding `Nat.add`" in 0.3-0.5 s: evaluation's own depth, before conversion.
- Steps rise by about one per sum walked below the top (+1-4% on the probes); `total_visits` fall (no `nesting` call). Bench baseline may move slightly where nested sums are compared.

New test `nested_sum_walks_a_plain_chain_once` (depth 400: 75k steps; 393k and 15 s with the record switched off, checked). Depth 1,000 runs out of stack in the test thread, in conv comparing the sums' arguments (opens-by-tree path, per level), not in reread.

Tests: `test:one -- nested_sum` (5 passed); `nat_add_rule::`, proof_equivalence wrapping + G2 probes, `the_known_gaps_hold_in_the_plain_evaluator` (11 passed). clippy core+elab clean, cargo fmt.

Findings: (1) a failed `rfl` on long stuck-sum chains renders its message with quadratic-or-worse evaluation (rep unequal 1,000: 90M steps, 3.4 s; 10,000 > 60 s), `check::refl_error` -> `Ctx::show`. (2) conv of two `Nat.add` chains recurses on the Rust stack per level (opens-by-tree argument compare), so depth ~1,000 is E-RESOURCE in a test thread.

Review follow-ups (Fable review docs/reviews/SW-2875-g2-walk-once-review.md, 11 Nov 2026):
- 4b, what made the `decreasing` unequal probe faster: the record, measured. Same build with the record switched off (a temporary env switch, since removed): dec unequal 10,000 took 23,728 ms and 214.8M steps (24.2 s); with it, 614 ms and 15.0M steps. rep equal 10,000 off: 9,145 / 9,204 ms, 201.3M steps; on: 42 / 30 ms, 1.33M. The review's reading (each walk of a chain built by unfolding unfolds something, so nothing is filed) holds only for the first walks. Traced at depth 1,000: 17 walks unfolded something (8,005 sums between them); the other 3,602 unfolded nothing and were filed (7,818 sums). Without the record, 7,918 such walks went over 2.0M sums. Most likely why (reasoned, not traced): the `decreasing` calls are glued calls that keep their unfoldings, and `view_with` forces them, so once the first walks have unfolded the chain, later walks see the plain sums under them and unfold nothing. So "34 s to 1.1 s" stands, from the record; the step charge and the loop add steps and don't save time.

tickets.title: [Opus] Readings with gluing off: at the use site the fact's type is an evaluated value, so unglued a user function's reading reads as its unfolding (And instead of InRange); build the reader on terms (written types, readings' statement terms) — SW-2977 review M2; also L1 (E-NO-READING should say the reading is declared later in the unit, and stay quiet when the reading failed) and L2 (readings on alias functions tiny := small: filed under tiny now; decide)
tickets.body:
Lane notes (Opus, 12 Nov 2026, 17:08-17:35, est. 2 h):

- **M2** (205b825bb): the reader evaluates with calls kept folded and, with gluing off, starts from the fact's type as written (variable's declared type, annotation, argument's parameter type, the definition's own type, match columns). Glued: unchanged (early return). Test: `elaboration readings::a_user_reading_is_found_{glued,unglued}`. Gap: an expected test fact with no written type to hand (e.g. a lambda body's expected type) still reads the unfolded value unglued.
- **L1** (8e7030550): `ItemInfo.reading` holds each `@[reading]` theorem's test function and polarity from its syntax; a use above it stops at the function with E-NO-READING "`inRange`'s reading, `inRangeReads`, is declared below" + label at the reading. A reading whose proof fails is filed as its D3527 stand-in, so users rely on it ("2 declarations rely on a declaration with an error"); with no stand-in, E-FAILED-DEPENDENCY (dropped beside the reading's own error). Examples: reject/reading-declared-below.sw, reject/reading-failed.sw.
- **L2** (5d9e12514), orchestrator-level call taken by the lane: refuse. A reading whose test passes the function more arguments than its definition takes (`def tiny: Nat → Bool := small`) is E-READING-SHAPE, since `tiny n` unfolds to `small n` before anything reads it and the reading was dead. Filing under `small` was rejected: it breaks E-READING-PLACE when `small` is elsewhere. Example: reject/reading-alias.sw.
- Kernel terms: glued, unchanged (hash_stability passes). Unglued, the reader's proof terms now hold folded calls (`inRangeReads lo x hi`), as glued ones do.
- Tests: readings:: (2 pass), test:example NAME=reading (7 pass), projects reading tests (6 pass), hash_stability (10 pass), running examples accepted|goal|rejected|soundness (7 pass).


Review fixes (cfa9f87c7, 17:42-17:52):
- M3/L1 unglued: `as_written` uses the written type only where it is convertible to the fact's type (resource errors propagate: L3), and reads refined variables from the context (`let h2 := h; match x with …`). Placeholder arguments (check.rs) pass the head up to the argument (`head_before_placeholder`), so `t x {..} {..}` checks each argument against its own parameter.
- L2: pending readings matched by the name the statement resolves to (`Elaborator::named`), or a dot form's function name (`b.ok`); `Iff (…) (…)` recognised.
- M1: `readings::a_helper_above_the_reading_that_it_uses_checks`, ignored (fails today with "can't be built with `Both` yet"), ready for the checking-order decision.
- Tests: readings:: 4 pass + the ignored one fails as expected (--run-ignored all); test:example NAME=reading 7 pass; running examples accepted|goal|rejected|soundness 7 pass; clippy elab + elaboration test target clean.


D3537 (Matt, 12 Nov 2026: 'Happy to go with your recommendations'): dependency order, not file position, decides which uses see a reading: uses wait for the reading via an ordering edge; the reading's own dependencies read by unfolding; no 'declared below'.

D3537 built (d1b6626c3, 18:22-18:36, est. 60 min; merged main first, 3152411bd):
- `reading_edges` (module.rs, before `instance_edges`, not in the library): each `@[reading]` item's test function resolved from its syntax (`f`, `Ns.f`, `x.f` by last name, `↔` or `Iff`); every Def/Test item depending on it, and not reached by the reading, gets a speculative edge to the reading. No cycles by construction.
- The "declared below" E-NO-READING is gone; `examples/reject/reading-declared-below.sw` became `examples/accept/reading-used-above.sw` (+ hash snapshot). A failed reading with no stand-in still gives the quiet E-FAILED-DEPENDENCY.
- In the reading's dependencies, a failed read gets a note: "`inRange`'s reading, `inRangeReads`, isn't available here: `inRangeReads` depends on this declaration, so here `inRange` reads as what it unfolds to" (no_reading, E-NOT-A-RECORD, the dot field fallback; not in the reading's own proof).
- Tests: readings:: 8 pass (helper above reading un-ignored, use above, Iff and dot forms from above, the why-note, two-file order both ways); test:example NAME=reading 7; projects reading 6; hash_stability 10 (new snapshot); examples accepted|goal|rejected|soundness 7.

Expected: 90 min. Started 18:55, done 19:08 (12 Nov 2026).

Cause: harness only. A declaration with an error stands in as a final assumption under its own name (SW-2952, D3527); check_attempt read accepted as Final && !marked_unfinished, so every stand-in `boom` (and `anything` built on one) was a finding. Old harness at VOID=20 seed 0x2c02: 534/534 rejected by load, 400 findings, all "boom was accepted".

Could a user rely on boom? No, on every path checked (file and two-namespace project with importer, each twice for the cache): check, audit, test, run, axioms all exit 1; audit fails boom ("has an error") and anything ("relies on `boom`, which has an error; checked assuming its statement"); test "five" not run (relies on boom); the check cache stores nothing for either.

Fix (lane/SW-3017, f86367df1): check_attempt skips Elaborator::is_unfinished(id) (final and relying on no assumption, as audit reads it).

Fuzz with the fix, seed 0x2c02: VOID=20 534 attempts 0 findings; VOID=1500 2014 attempts (29 accepted) 0 findings, 68 s.
Tests: proofs stand_ins:: (1 pass); tools test_json::|audit:: (49 pass).

Two questions: why the effects analysis change alters what the JIT compiles (it was meant to give identical answers), and why a 32-bit PC-relative reference reaches a symbol >2 GiB away
tickets.body:
Lane (Opus, 13 Nov 2026, 16:57-17:10, est. 2 h): branch lane/SW-3139, commit ae340838a.

- Effects: ba4e20071 changes no answer. The old may_perform_at was run beside the new one and both answers and visit counts compared: 294,521 calls over the prelude (hash_stability::prelude), plus the n1 tests and the effect examples (about 14,000 more). No difference. So no effects fix: the bisect landed on a commit that only moved where things got mapped.
- Relocation: the X86PCRel4 is the `lea` for the body's name data (`{symbol}.name`, the count_bodies instrumentation: first_part's symbol_value). The data was declared Linkage::Local, so `colocated`, so PC-relative. cranelift-jit's SystemMemoryProvider mmaps code and data separately with no nearness guarantee (likely culprit for the distance: the tests' 16 GiB with_stack thread stack, with holes above and below it). Fix: n1::far_data marks the reference not colocated, so it is a movabs/Abs8 (x86-64) or literal load (aarch64). Calls between JIT functions are fine: cranelift-jit veneers out-of-range calls. Helpers are Import and already Abs8.
- Test: n1::tests::code_reads_data_mapped_far_away maps data 8 GiB from code; it panics in cranelift-jit with the data colocated (aarch64 adrp arm, compiled_blob.rs:324) and passes with the fix. bodies_count_their_entries_when_asked also asserts no `symbol colocated` in its listing.
- Needs Linux verification: n1::bodies_count_their_entries_when_asked and n1::tests::code_reads_data_mapped_far_away on Overmind.
Verified on Linux x86_64 by Overmind at 664e62326: both tests pass (the n1 test failed 20/20 before). Model result: Opus, worked (plus a libc dev-dependency fixup for Linux), 12 min (est. 120).

In debug, reject (parser-count-differs-from-lemma notes, reads-nested-binds-unknown-field E-RESOURCE) and nesting (two small-guard tests) fail identically with the direct route forced (checked with a temporary env switch), so they are pre-existing debug-only stack limits, not this change.
